name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: a sourced discount, a higher auto run-rate and a HOLD
frontmatter.summary: Revision answers the red team: the holdco discount is reset to the method card midpoint instead of the share price, the listed stakes are marked at dated closes, the auto block is marked at the third-quarter exit and the buyback runs through the authorised amount. Target Rp4,723, expected return 2.5%: HOLD.
thesis: The parts are worth Rp4,433 per share after a 30% discount taken from the method card's range, not from the share price; the discount is the base rate and the target is an output [S0, S15, S21, S22, S23].
The base is the most likely path: the actual nine months, the Q3 auto exit confirmed by October wholesales, capex at the audited line and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14, S15, S20, S6].

The market price implies a discount at the floor of the card's range, so the target sits below the price; the expected return of 2.5% is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend, not a discount recovery [S0, S15].
The tails are mirrored inside the card range and weighted by likelihood, bear heavier than bull: 30% at Rp4,107 and 25% at Rp5,401 around a 45% base at Rp4,756 [S15, S14].
No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists: the authorised buyback is undated and related-party purchases are untested, so the HOLD does not rest on a narrowing view [S8, S16, S6, F21].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: No dated discount-narrowing catalyst exists. The buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and ongoing with no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16]; the dated capital-allocation event is the Otoparts tender close, which lifts an already consolidated stake rather than upstreaming value to the holdco [S13, S14].

blocks.text: **What changed.** Four input corrections. First, the base discount is now 30%, the midpoint of the method card's persistent range, no longer solved from the share price: the prior 21.0% was the print at Rp5,000, which made the target a roll of the close [S0, S15]. Second, the listed stakes are marked at dated 6 November 2026 closes — United Tractors at Rp23,025, Astra Agro Lestari at Rp9,450 and Astra Graphia at Rp2,500 [S21, S22, S23]. Third, the automotive block is marked at the third-quarter exit, not the diluted nine-month average [S14, F68, F32, S20]. Fourth, the buyback runs through the authorised IDR8.00tn at the completed pace [S14, F65].

**The call.** Target Rp4,723 against Rp5,000, an expected total return of 2.5% including Rp400 of dividends: **HOLD**. The base path is Rp4,756; the bear Rp4,107 at 30% and the bull Rp5,401 at 25%. The target sits below the price because we no longer assume the market's discount is the base rate.

**Variant view.** On our marks the price implies 21.0%, at the floor of the method card's range. We hold the midpoint because no dated catalyst supports floor pricing: the only named narrowing action is an undated buyback [S8, S14, S16]. The market already pays most of what the parts are worth after the base-rate discount, so the return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend.

**Bias audit, signed.** Optimistic on the target: auto at the Q3 exit, confirmed by October wholesales [S20, F101, F102]; buyback at the completed pace; the FY2027E gross margin back to the FY2025 rate; and the FY2026E minority take of 11.0% against the audited IDR7,436.0bn on IDR40,205.0bn [S15, S6]. Conservative on the target: the 30% base sits above the 21.0% the price implies; the implied fourth quarter is below the third quarter's clean run-rate; and capex is at the audited IDR18.46tn rather than the lower data-pack figure. Net: the discount is the largest single departure and it is a headwind against the price; the operating items are sourced and near the last actual. We do not call the stack balanced.

Astra International is a listed portfolio of subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. It reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as three core businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3]. FY2025 parent net income split Automotive IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, heavy equipment and mining IDR9.10tn, agribusiness IDR1.17tn, infrastructure IDR1.26tn, IT IDR0.21tn and property IDR0.72tn [S4]. The 2026 strategy placed wider businesses under an earn-or-reallocate test [S11]; Jardine Cycle & Carriage controls 50.1% on a 43.0% free float [S6, S0].

The October print is the delta. National wholesales reached 760,476 units over ten months and 81,482 in October, 31.2% on October 2025 and 2.4% on September, with retail sales of 758,653 units [S20]. The run-rate is at the top of the observers' 890,000 to 930,000 range [S20, S9].

The article's growth headline is not usable. Its ten-month comparative of 561,405 units does not reconcile with its own October 2025 figure of 62,090 or with the nine-month print of 679,000 [S20, F106, F104, F59]; the true ten-month growth is consistent with the monthly series, far below the headline. We use the monthly units, and the re-rating is not attributed to the print: the base discount is no longer taken from the post-print price, so that challenge is answered by construction [S0, S20].

The mix is the structural story. LCGC wholesales were 83,997 units in the first nine months, a -11.0% change, about one car in eight against roughly one in six a year earlier [S18, F59]. ACC attributes the fall to buyers trading up with LCGC underwriting unchanged, which we treat as the primary cause because the group distributes the up-class nameplates too [S18]. The structural channel is Chinese electric models priced at LCGC levels: national EV wholesales reached 101,171 units in the first eight months, double the 50,749 a year earlier and almost the whole of FY2025's 103,931 [S9].

The mining complex turned in the third quarter. Over nine months Komatsu units fell to 3,000 and overburden to 766.0 million bank cubic metres; coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped [S14]. The division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14].

Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles; the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm captive origination [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese and electrified entrants, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The state sets the coal quota and vehicle taxes shape demand [S14, S9]; the house macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and inflation at 3.3% [KB macro deck, 2026].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, held back by the Martabe outage and the coal quota; the third quarter ran at a better margin as mining and gold recovered [S15, S14]. Selling and administrative expenses of IDR10.41tn and IDR16.94tn rose faster than revenue, so operating profit fell [S15]. Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, of which IDR2.96tn was non-recurring impairment and fair-value charges; clean net profit was IDR24.57tn [S15, S14].

Two source labels are corrected. The 30 September 2026 accounts are **unaudited** — the filing says "tidak diaudit" — so the gearing, parent debt and book figures drawn from them are interim and only the FY2025 accounts carry an audit opinion [S15, S14, S6]. Capex is now the audited expenses-by-nature line of IDR18.46tn, not the data pack's IDR18,464.0bn, and it is no longer called an audited ratio on the data-pack figure [S6, F111, S0]. Depreciation is restated from the audited notes at IDR17.87tn for FY2025 and IDR16.70tn for FY2024 [S6]; FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, a margin of 17.5% [S6]. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn, above consolidated profit as financing receivables grew [S15, S14].

Group net debt was IDR56,315.0bn at FY2025 [S0]; almost all of it sits in the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn at 30 September 2026, leaving group net cash of IDR1.80tn excluding them [S14]. The bridge uses parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn, plus lease liabilities of IDR0.06tn and IDR0.36tn [S15] — so the group net-debt forecast does not drive the target.

**Actual versus forecast.** The nine-month actual sets the roll: revenue IDR243.87tn and clean profit IDR24.57tn against FY2026E IDR329,859.8bn and IDR33,081.7bn [S15, S14]. The model's implied fourth quarter is the annual line less the nine-month actual, and it sits below the third quarter's clean run-rate; this is the one unsourced conservatism in the earnings build, it does not feed the SOTP, and we disclose it rather than describe the quarter as needing only the run-rate [S15, S14, F48]. We carry revenue growth of 2.0%, a gross margin of 21.7% and costs at 11.1% of revenue [S15, S0, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate while costs stay at the sourced nine-month 11.2% [S15, S6], consistent with a smaller low-margin LCGC mix and with nine-month automotive income of IDR9.79tn already up on the prior year [S14]. The minority take is 11.0% this year and 18.0% long run, toward the FY2025 audited rate as mining recovers [S15, S6]. Net income to the parent is IDR33,081.7bn, IDR33,184.3bn and IDR39,502.2bn [S15, S6].

Earnings quality, at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2023-FY2025 [S0] and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15]. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and stripped before the SOTP, while the P/E cross-check uses reported LTM [S14, S0]. **Cost divergence** is real and we hold the nine-month ratio rather than bank operating leverage [S15]. **Financing provisioning** was built at IDR1.16tn in the first half against receivables of IDR132.00tn [S5, F35, F60]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases of IDR84.94tn were about a quarter of revenue and sales IDR27.94tn under a tenth, with no transfer-pricing test possible on consolidated accounts [S6]. **Revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn, and no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum of the parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.6% and WACC 11.9%, from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.32 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.59), a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% and country risk of 2.5% [KB macro deck, 2026; house config].

**The marks now carry dates.** The listed stakes go in at the 6 November 2026 close, not a stale pack price: United Tractors at Rp23,025 on the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at Rp9,450 on 79.7% and Astra Graphia at Rp2,500 on 76.9% [S21, S22, S23, S6]. The prior marks used the sibling packs' 26 October closes for UNTR and ASGR, stale by the time of the November print; the assumptions disclose each value with its price, share count and date. The unlisted blocks use section-level marks, not one blanket multiple [S0, S2]. The automotive block is marked on the third-quarter exit, not the diluted nine-month average: nine-month attributable income was IDR9.79tn, H1 was IDR5.91tn, so Q3 alone earned the difference, an annualised run-rate materially above the nine-month annualisation, and October wholesales of 81,482 were in line with the Q3 monthly average [S14, S5, S20]. The value effect is a material uplift to the auto block and to NAV per share, the largest single correction to the parts. The section multiple is the mean of Astra Otoparts' forward and Selamat Sempurna's LTM market P/E from the house data packs, disclosed as a forward/LTM mix; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November [S19] and the SMSM price date is in the assumptions [S25].

The financing block is on its own book/ROE-COE card: income includes the segment's joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn against liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. We normalise the annualised return for a fourth quarter at the first-half provisioning pace; the block earns above the 14.6% cost of equity and is carried at a justified premium to book, while a repeat first-half-size charge would take the return to the cost of equity and the mark to book [S5, F35, F60]. The infrastructure block is marked on the group's own five-year average P/E of 7.2x, not a toll-road peer multiple: no toll-road pack exists in coverage, the label is corrected, and the block is small [S0, S4, F7]. Property uses the listed-property peer median applied to recurring income after stripping the IDR0.46tn bargain-purchase gain [S6, F29, F9]. Parent G&A sits inside the auto mark because the parent is an operating distributor [S15].

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: P/E gives Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686, 22.4% and 50.8% above the sum of the parts [S0]. They are undiscounted while the parts carry a 30% discount, P/BV uses the 30 September book of IDR238.10tn [S15], and the averages were struck when mining earned far more — H1-2025 mining profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5].

**The discount is the base rate.** The base holds 30%, the midpoint of the method card's persistent range, applied to the marks and independent of the share price. The card says holdco discounts persist indefinitely by default and that cheapness alone is not a thesis; a market-implied 21.0% is at the floor of that range, not a base rate. The midpoint also sits inside the disclosed CONGLOMERATES peer set, where ADRO, BRPT and CUAN trade near the low thirties, DSSA and TOBA at forty per cent and BNMR at thirty-eight [cov_publish comps]. Two name-specific facts argue against the floor: no dated narrowing catalyst — the authorised buyback has no end date or pace [S8, S14, S16] — and related-party purchases of IDR84.94tn, a structural and untested flow that widens the warranted discount [S6]. Upstream cover is above one, with parent profit of IDR19.89tn against IDR16.43tn of dividends paid, so the discount is not argued from dividend distress [S6, F98, F22].

**Target construction.** The base compounds the blended mark of Rp4,498 at the 14.6% cost of equity and nets Rp400 of dividends, giving Rp4,756; weighting base 45%, bear 30% at Rp4,107 and bull 25% at Rp5,401 gives Rp4,723 [S15, S0]. There is no discount-convergence term. The weights are likelihood-based: the bear is the heavier tail because a move back to the top of the card range needs no catalyst, while the bull requires the undated buyback to be read as one [S8, S14, S16].

**What the price implies.** At Rp5,000 the market capitalises the parts at a 21.0% discount, the bottom of the card's range. That is a fair place for a holdco with no dated catalyst to sit, and it is why the target is below the price: we hold the base rate, not the print. No historical sum-of-parts NAV exists, so the closest own series is P/B, which has averaged 1.1x over FY2022A-FY2025A and stands at 0.9x today [S0] — a cheapness signal, not a catalyst.

**The scenario engine has a disclosed limit.** The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every case, so the bear's revenue, margin and share-count shocks do not reprice the parts. The tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity, not a full earnings stress. Two marks that are not repriced carry more than half of gross value: the two commodity stakes and the financing book [S14, S15]. A true bear that marked the financing arm at book after a repeat of the H1 provisioning pace would remove about IDR1.16tn of annualised income capitalised at the segment multiple, and a share loss in autos would cut the auto block further; neither is in the table, and we say so rather than publishing a target the report calls an overstatement [S5, F35, F60]. The published bear is still a live path: coal and gold do not recover, credit costs rise, autos lose share, and the discount returns to the top of the card range [S14, S9, S8].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever, and coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings [S14, S9, S4].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand [KB macro deck, 2026]; a consumer-financing group is exposed on demand and credit [S2, S4]. That caution is in the country risk premium and in a normalised financing premium.

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese and electrified entrants threaten the auto franchise, met through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; a share or mix loss is the largest value risk, and the bear's operating shocks are the only place it is counted [S9, S14].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block carries IDR66.70tn of net debt against receivables of IDR132.00tn. Repeating the IDR1.16tn first-half charge inside one quarter would cut the block's return to the cost of equity and the mark to book; the engine does not reprice the mark in a scenario [S5, S14, F35].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8].
**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR244.7bn a day, parent profit covered the FY2025 dividend, and the interim held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10].

The base (45%) carries the actual nine months, the Q3 auto exit, the nine-month cost ratio, a minority take near the audited level, the discount at 30% with no narrowing, and buyback retirement at the completed pace [S14, S20]; it gives Rp4,756. The bull (25%) assumes Astra's share recovers toward the company's 51.0% target, the coal quota resets, the wider-business roadmap adds earnings, and the buyback narrows the discount to the floor of the card range [S14, S11, S18]. The bear (30%) runs the mining non-recovery, a credit-cost rise, an auto share loss and a discount back to the top of the range [S14, S5, S9]. The discount shocks are mirrored; the probabilities are not, because the narrowing catalyst is undated.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Buyback execution at the completed pace through the authorised amount, a dated capital-allocation event that upstreams cash, October-November share data showing Astra holding its share, and financing provisioning that stays at the H1 pace rather than rising [S14, S20, S5].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage held 50.1% at the last audited date, part of the Jardine Matheson group, on a 43.0% free float [S0, S6]; no pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed [S6]. Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Toyota, Daihatsu and Honda joint ventures; the purchase ratio fell from 32.8% of cost while the gross margin held, but the consolidated accounts do not permit a transfer-pricing test, so the flow is structural and untested — a discount-widening fact, not a clean bill [S6]. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026 and the IDR8.00tn programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. The Otoparts tender at Rp3,600 for up to 4.95 per cent lifts the stake to 84.95 per cent, a maximum of IDR0.86tn [S13, S14]; AUTO closed at Rp3,260 on 4 November, so the offer is a small transfer from the parent to minorities [S19]. On ESG the material exposures are coal, palm oil, nickel and the vehicle transition, met through Japanese partners rather than a platform the group owns [S14, S9].

**Audit and listing status.** The FY2025 accounts carry blank pages where the auditor's report sits and name no audit firm, and no source states the IDX board or a notation, so both remain open checks; no adverse opinion or special notation appears anywhere we read, but absence of evidence is not a clean bill [S6].

The dated catalysts are the Otoparts tender close, the monthly wholesale data and the FY2026 audited results, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S13, S20, S4]. None is a dated discount-narrowing catalyst, which is why the base holds the card midpoint and the rating is HOLD [S8, S14].

We monitor the ten-month run-rate of 760,476 and Astra's monthly share, which the October print does not disclose [S20, F57]; the LCGC versus up-class split [S18]; Komatsu units and overburden [S14]; financing receivables and provisioning [S14, S5]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and parent profit against dividends paid [S6].

bear.narrative: The national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the mining complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales down to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. Financial-services credit costs rise as a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears: the financing book carried a Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60]; a repeat inside one quarter takes the block's ROE to the cost of equity and its mark toward book, about Rp6.2tn that the holdco_sotp engine does not reprice. The auto franchise loses share and mix to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9], the buyback stops so the share count drifts up, and the holdco discount widens back to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, from the 30% midpoint [S8, S14]. The bear widens the discount by 10pp, a mirrored move to the range top. The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity: a true bear that also marks the financing arm at book and reprices United Tractors and Astra Agro Lestari below their market marks would be below the figure shown here. That depth is disclosed in section 5 and is not used to justify the bear's weight.

bull.narrative: The market leg is already printed, not assumed: ten-month wholesales reached 760,476 units and October ran at 81,482 [S20, F101, F102], so the bull's incremental industry assumption is that Astra's 49% share recovers toward the company's 51% target [S14, F57, F14] rather than that the market reaches its range, with Astra taking the up-class volume it is already selling [S18]. The national coal quota resets and the mining complex stabilises (this is a bull assumption, not in the base), the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap add earnings - nine-month Others attributable profit was already Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S11, S14, F71] - share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount from the 30% midpoint to 20%, the bottom of the card's persistent range: we do not assume a break below the range without a dated catalyst, and the undated buyback is not one [S8, S14, S16]. The bull narrows the discount by 10pp, the mirror of the bear. The share-count shock carries the buyback acceleration; the Otoparts tender (maximum about Rp858bn [S13, F89]) and the Others run-rate sit above the table because the consolidated marks already carry their earnings. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark in this case, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +2%: the nine-month actual was Rp243,869bn [S15] and the third quarter alone Rp85,956bn, ahead of the second quarter's Rp79,245bn; management guides the fourth quarter to be supported by the same drivers that lifted the third - mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued automotive growth [S14]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate gives full-year revenue of about Rp329.8tn, or +2% on FY2025. The 2% is therefore the last actual and the company's guided continuation, not a step-up beyond it. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.70%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% (gross profit Rp19,556bn on revenue Rp85,956bn) [S15, S0]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue rather than the bare 11.22% nine-month ratio. The prior 10.14% FY2025 ratio no longer describes the run-rate. From FY2027E held at the sourced nine-month 11.22% [S15]: the nine-month cost ratio is the last full actual, the third quarter alone (10.84%) is the best quarter and is not the run-rate, and no sourced cost programme justifies reverting to the pre-2026 10.14% ratio. The forecast therefore carries the higher nine-month run-rate, not the best quarter.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual from the expenses-by-nature note, capex Rp18,464bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn, or 5.71% [S6, F111]; the data pack's Rp17,440bn is a different capex definition and is not used now that the audited line is sourced. The group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised further.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11%, the full-year rate implied by the actual nine months plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's minority take: clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn (reported Rp24,073bn plus the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge) with about Rp2,471bn to non-controlling interests, a 9.1% clean take [S12, S14, S15]; the third quarter alone carried Rp1,660bn to minorities on Rp10,729bn of profit, a 15.5% take, as United Tractors' mining recovery lifted the 40.5% minority share [S0, S15]. A fourth quarter at that rate gives a full-year take of about 11%. The mining business collapsed in the first half while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 17% and 18% long run, close to the FY2025 audited 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]): the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take just below that 18.5% actual, not at the 15% used before, which assumed the mining recovery accrued disproportionately to the parent. The UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and share count.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Set at the company-reported FY2025 payout ratio of 48% on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4, F90], not the 50% parent-entity cash payout (Rp16,426bn of parent cash dividends over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]) that was used before: the 48% is the policy ratio the company itself states, and the 50% is a parent-entity cash-flow ratio that mixes parent dividend income and one-off items. The same Rp98 interim was declared for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -4.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] is carried to completion at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65], which is about Rp0.9tn a month. Rp8tn at that pace retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, in roughly nine months, inside FY2027E. The prior 2.0% truncated the programme after one year for no sourced reason and understated the only holdco-level capital return the company is actually executing; the remaining uncertainty is timing, not the pace, and the bull carries no extra retirement.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 30%, the midpoint of the holdco method card's persistent 20-40% discount range, independent of the share price: the target is an output of the marks and this discount, not a reproduction of the 6 November close [S0]. The card says holdco discounts of 20-40% persist indefinitely by default and that cheapness alone is not a thesis; a 16.46% market-implied level is outside that range and is therefore not a base rate. The 30% midpoint also sits in the disclosed CONGLOMERATES peer set, where ADRO, BRPT and CUAN trade at about 30%, DSSA and TOBA at 40% and BNMR at 38% [cov_publish comps], and it is supported by two name-specific facts that argue against the 20% floor: there is no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM carries no end date or disclosed pace [S8, S14, S16]) and related-party purchases were Rp84.9tn, about a quarter of FY2025 revenue, a structural and untested flow that the method card says widens the warranted discount [S6, F21]. Upstream cover is above one on the parent's own accounts - FY2025 profit for the year of Rp19,886bn against Rp16,426bn of dividends paid [S6, F98, F22] - so the discount is not argued from dividend distress. This replaces the price-derived 16.46%: the discount is now the base rate, and the observed market level is reported only as what today's price implies.

challenges.challenge: The 96%-weighted SOTP is calibrated to reproduce the share price, so the target is not a valuation. NAV per share is 5,985.0; the discount is solved as 1 - 5,000/5,985.0 = 16.46%, which returns exactly 4,999.9, the 6 November close [S0, S15, fund record]. The base is then v0 5,042.1 x (1 + 14.63%) - 400 = 5,379.9, i.e. price x (1 + COE) - DPS plus the 4% cross-check premium. The 21.83% -> 16.46% move is therefore not a sourced discount path but the price move itself (4,680 -> 5,000), the exact loop the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card step 2 forbids: the discount is the base rate, not the opportunity. The report says as much: "solving for the discount that reproduces Rp5,000 gives 16.5%." A fundamental NAV of 5,985 never enters as an independent number.
challenges.answer: The discount is no longer solved from the price. The base is 30%, the midpoint of the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT persistent range, applied to the marks; the SOTP is an output (Rp4,433 per share after discount, Rp6,333 NAV per share) and the target is Rp4,723, below the Rp5,000 close. The 16.46% price-derived level is withdrawn; the market-implied discount is reported only as what the price implies.

challenges.challenge: The base holds a 16.46% discount that is below the method card's persistent 20-40% range and below every CONGLOMERATES peer (ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA 40%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN 30%, BNMR 38%, IMJS 60%), with no dated narrowing catalyst [cov_publish comps]. The card says 20-40% persists indefinitely by default and cheapness alone is not a thesis. Holding the current print as the most likely twelve-month discount is an optimistic base: a return to the card's 20% floor alone lowers the SOTP to 4,788 and the target to about 4,948. The report's defence is that the observed level is the market's, which is the C1 circularity, not a sourced path.
challenges.answer: Base discount moved inside the card range to the 30% midpoint, supported by the peer set (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN about 30%, DSSA/TOBA 40%, BNMR 38%), the absence of a dated narrowing catalyst and the untested related-party flow. The 20% floor is the bull destination (Rp5,401) and the 40% top the bear destination (Rp4,107), so both ends of the range are shown.

challenges.challenge: The auto block, 40% of gross value, is marked on 9M attributable income annualised at 4/3 (9,787 x 4/3 = 13,049) x 7.357 = 96,004 [S15, F68]. The Q3 alone carried about 3,873 of auto income (9M 9,787 less H1 5,914 [F32]), an annualised 15,492, 19% above the 9M average and 16% above the mark. October national wholesales of 81,482 were 1.0% above the Q3 monthly average of 80,673, so the Q3 exit is the current run-rate, not a spike. At the Q3 exit the block is worth about 113,977, roughly Rp453/share more NAV (about Rp173 on the target after the 0.4 base weight).
challenges.answer: Auto block marked at the Q3 exit: 9M Rp9,787bn less H1 Rp5,914bn gives Q3 Rp3,873bn, annualised Rp15,492bn; the multiple on the 9M fact is 11.6456x (7.357 x 4/3 x the Q3-exit ratio). October wholesales of 81,482 confirm the exit. Gross value rises by about Rp18tn.

challenges.challenge: The buyback is truncated. The model carries share_change -1.3% FY2026E, -2.0% FY2027E and zero from FY2028E [assumptions share_change]. The Rp8tn approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM [S8, S16] at the completed Rp10.0tn/eleven-month pace [S14, F65] retires about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the 39.69bn count, roughly double the 2.0% carried. The report calls the buyback undated (true) but the completed pace is sourced, and the method card lists a holdco-level buyback as a qualifying catalyst; the base gives it half the observed run-rate.
challenges.answer: Buyback carried through the authorised Rp8tn at the completed Rp10tn/eleven-month pace: FY2027E share change -4.0% (about 1.6bn shares, 4.0% of the count) instead of -2.0%, with no further retirement assumed after that.

challenges.challenge: The financing block is 26% of gross value (62,607) and is marked at 1.109x book on a normalised 16.0% ROE [assumptions holdings]. A repeat of the H1 provisioning pace in one quarter, or a credit-cost rise, takes ROE to the 14.82% cost of equity and the mark to book (1.0x), removing about 6,154bn or Rp155/share [S5, F35, F60]. The report admits "a true bear ... would be below the tabulated Rp3,878, so the target of Rp5,041 overstates a true-bear-weighted target" but publishes 5,041 anyway. With the two commodity stakes repriced as the report describes, the true bear is near 3,533 and the true-bear-weighted target about 4,938, some Rp100 (2%) lower than the published 5,041.
challenges.answer: The financing-to-book de-rate is now stated in section 5 as a value the tabulated bear does not carry, with the H1 provisioning fact and the ROE-to-COE mechanism; the report no longer publishes a target it calls an overstatement. The holdco_sotp engine cannot reprice holdings in a scenario, so the de-rate is disclosed rather than tabulated.

challenges.challenge: The report calls an auto share or mix loss "the largest value risk", but the bear's four shocks (discount +23.54pp, revenue -3pp, gross margin -1.2pp, share change +1.5pp) do not reprice the 40%-weight auto block; the holdco_sotp engine marks it on fixed 9M income, so the tabulated bear moves only through the discount and the 2%/2% cross-checks. A 2pp share loss (49% to 47%) on a ~923k market is about 18,460 units, roughly 4% of ASII volume and about 3,840bn of auto mark, and the Chinese-EV substitution channel the report itself sizes [S9, F93-F95] is larger. None of it is in the bear.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now states plainly that the tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity and cannot be read as a full earnings stress; the auto share/mix loss is named as the largest value risk but is not repriced by the engine, and that limitation is disclosed rather than implied.

challenges.challenge: The discount compression is attributed to the October print, but the report itself rejects that print's +35.5% headline: the 561,405 comparator is the nine-month 2025 base, and the true 10M growth against a consistent base is about 22.0% (760,476 vs 561,174 + 62,090) [S20, F26, F104, F106]. If the market traded the erroneous +35.5% headline to Rp5,000, the re-rating may be overdone by the 13.5pp gap. The report uses the post-print price to set the base discount (16.46%) without testing the pre-print 21.83% level or the true growth rate.
challenges.answer: The erroneous +35.5% headline is rejected and the true growth is taken from the monthly series; the base discount is no longer taken from the post-print price, so the re-rating is not used to set value. The pre-print 21.83% level is no longer a base candidate because the base is the card midpoint.

challenges.challenge: The "balanced departures" claim is not signed and in part inverted. Section 4 says the base "mixes sourced departures rather than a one-way haircut: the observed discount, capex at the FY2025 audited ratio and terminal growth below nominal GDP are offset by the auto block's nine-month annualisation, the minority take and the FY2027E margin reversion." But the auto block's 4/3 annualisation is a haircut against the Q3 exit (C3), not an offset; the observed discount is the most optimistic input (C2); the 11% minority take and the 22.09% margin reversion are optimistic; capex 17,440 is not the audited 18,464 [S6]. The net sign is not shown, and the list is presented as balance.
challenges.answer: The departures are now signed individually (optimistic, conservative, neutral) with the net stated; the auto annualisation and the observed discount are removed from the offset column, and the report no longer calls the stack balanced.

challenges.challenge: The Q4 net-income build is below the Q3 clean run-rate. 9M clean parent profit was 24,565 [F48]; H1 clean was 14,892 (reported 12,533 plus 2,359 non-recurring [S2]); Q3 clean is therefore about 9,673, but the FY2026E np_parent of 33,081.7 implies Q4 of 8,517, 12% below Q3 [model lines]. Management explicitly guides the Q4 to be supported by the same drivers that lifted Q3 - mining-contract volumes and the Martabe restart [S14]. The report says "the fourth quarter needs only the third quarter's run-rate", which understates the model: it needs materially less. The conservatism is small on the target (SOTP ignores it) but it is unsourced and misdescribed.
challenges.answer: The "needs only the third quarter run-rate" sentence is corrected: the implied Q4 is the annual line less the nine-month actual and sits below the Q3 clean run-rate, disclosed as the one unsourced conservatism. It is not raised because no source supports a higher Q4 than the Q3 exit, and it does not feed the SOTP.

challenges.challenge: The 30/30 tail weights are not likelihood-based. The bear destination (40%) is the top of the card's persistent range; the bull destination (10%) is below the range floor. A return to the range is the card's default and is more probable than a break below it, so equal weights overstate the bull. The report says "neither tail has a dated trigger ... so there is no sourced reason to make one tail more likely", but the card's range is exactly that reason, and the QC justification itself admits the range is "not a registered source." At the same destinations, bear 35/bull 25 gives a target near 4,948, and bear 40/bull 20 near 4,854.
challenges.answer: Tail weights are now likelihood-based: base 45%, bear 30%, bull 25%, with the bear heavier because a return to the top of the card range needs no catalyst while the bull needs the undated buyback. Discount shocks are mirrored at +/-10pp to the 40% top and 20% floor.

challenges.challenge: The listed stakes, 29.6% of gross value (UNTR 54,248, AALI 14,492, ASGR 2,468), "go in at market [S6]" [report line 82; assumptions holdings], but S6 is the FY2025 audited accounts and carries the stakes, not the market prices. The marks actually used are the sibling datapacks' closes, and no price source or date is cited anywhere in fund record or fund record [S6, S0]. This is the prior QC Q2, unfixed. The same gap covers the auto block's 7.357x (AUTO/SMSM packs), the property peer median 5.79x (CTRA/PWON/SMRA/BSDE/ASRI, none of which has a model in coverage), and the toll-road 7.20138x (which is ASII's own five-year P/E, not a TOLL_ROADS multiple [model own_history]).
challenges.answer: Each listed stake now has a dated price source: UNTR Rp23,025, AALI Rp9,450 and ASGR Rp2,500 at the 6 November 2026 close [S21, S22, S23], with explicit values in the assumptions. The infrastructure multiple is relabelled as the group own five-year P/E, not a TOLL_ROADS mark; the auto multiple is disclosed as a forward/LTM mix with AUTO and SMSM price dates; the property peer packs are named with their price dates.

challenges.challenge: Two source labels are wrong. Section 3 says "the audited gearing note puts consolidated net debt at IDR64.92tn at 30 September 2026 [S15]" [report line 66], but S14 states the 9M financials are unaudited ("tidak diaudit") and only S6 is audited. Separately, capex of 17,440 is cited to S6 [report line 64; assumptions capex_pct], but S6's expenses-by-nature note shows capital expenditure of 18,464 [S6]; 17,440 is the data-pack figure [S0]. Section 4 then calls 17,440 "the FY2025 audited ratio". The numbers used are not wrong on the data pack, but the audit-quality claim and the S6 citation are.
challenges.answer: The 30 September 2026 accounts are labelled unaudited throughout; capex is restated to the audited S6 line of Rp18,464bn (fact F111) and the capex ratio is 5.71%, with the data-pack Rp17,440bn no longer used or called audited.

challenges.challenge: The update is a rewritten initiation passed off as a delta. It is 4,721 words against the 500-3,500 house update range (35% over), and grew from 4,244 in v11 despite the prior QC request to cut about 750 words [cov_report lint; prior review Q4]. Sections 1 (business description) and 6 (governance/ESG) are unchanged background, not the October delta; the investment summary alone is four long paragraphs. The title ("a stronger car market, a narrower discount and the same marginal HOLD") promises an update but the body re-argues the whole thesis.
challenges.answer: Report cut to 3,277 lint words (from 4,721), inside the 500-3,500 update range; sections 1 and 6 are compressed to the changed facts, the investment summary is four short paragraphs, and the body is the October delta, the 9M actual, the discount reset and the scenario vector.

missing_bull_case.note: Two absent. (1) The auto block is 40% of gross value (96,004 of 240,354) and is marked on 9M attributable income annualised at 4/3 (13,049), 16% below the Q3 exit rate of 15,492 and below the Q3-only run implied by segment income [S15, F68, F32]. October wholesales were 81,482 against a Q3 monthly average of 80,673, so the Q3 exit is the current run-rate, yet the block carries the diluted 9M average with no sourced reason. (2) The Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is carried at -2.0% in FY2027E and zero thereafter [S8, S16]; at the completed Rp10.0tn/eleven-month pace the authorised amount retires about 4.3% of the 39.69bn shares, roughly double the model [S14, F65].

missing_bear_case.note: Three absent or uncounted. (1) The financing block (62,607, 26% of gross) is marked at 1.109x book on a normalised 16.0% ROE; a credit-cost rise to the 14.8% cost of equity takes it to book, about 6,154bn or Rp155/share [S5, F35, F60]. The report discloses that a true bear would be below the tabulated 3,878 but still publishes a target built on the tabulated number. (2) The auto share/mix loss the report calls the largest value risk has no numeric effect: the bear's revenue and margin shocks do not reprice the 40%-weight auto mark, so the bear is a discount-only scenario. (3) Related-party purchases are 26% of revenue and untested [S6, F21], a method-card governance fact that widens the warranted discount, yet the base holds the narrowest discount in the peer set.

assumption_realism.note: The 16.46% base discount is the current print, not a most-likely path. The method card says 20-40% discounts persist by default; 16.46% sits below that range and 14-52pp below every CONGLOMERATES peer (ABMM 68.9%, DSSA/TOBA 40%, ADRO/BRPT/CUAN 30%, BNMR 38%), with no dated narrowing catalyst. The Q4 net-income build is also below the Q3 clean run-rate (8,517 vs about 9,673 implied by 9M clean 24,565 less H1 clean 14,892 [S2, S14]) even though management guides the same Q3 drivers to continue [S14].

evidence_and_citations.note: Three load-bearing gaps. (1) The listed stakes - 29.6% of gross value - "go in at market [S6]", but S6 is the FY2025 audited accounts and carries stakes, not prices; the marks actually used are the sibling datapacks' closes and no price source or date is cited [S6, S0]. This is the prior QC Q2, unfixed. (2) Section 3 calls the 30 September 2026 LK "audited" [S15]; S14 states the 9M accounts are unaudited ("tidak diaudit"), and capex 17,440 is cited to S6 although S6 shows 18,464 [S6]. (3) The infrastructure block is valued at 7.20138x labelled the "TOLL_ROADS house card's own-history multiple", but that number is ASII's own five-year P/E [model own_history]; no toll-road pack exists (JSMR has no model). The auto 7.357x blends AUTO 6.55x (a forward multiple, not LTM) with SMSM 8.17x (FY2025A LTM) [AUTO/SMSM packs].

valuation_method_fit.note: The method is SOTP but the primary method has no independent value: the 96%-weighted SOTP is NAV x (1 - discount) with the discount solved so the result equals the price (5,985.0 x 0.8354 = 4,999.9), so the base target is mechanically price x (1 + COE) - DPS plus the 4% cross-check premium. The fundamental NAV only enters through the price. The scenario spread is also a discount spread: the mirrored operating shocks move the target only through the 2%/2% cross-checks. And the card's dated-catalyst test is not met: the only named narrowing action is the undated Rp8tn buyback [S8, S16], and the Otoparts tender dates a subsidiary-level transfer to minorities, not value upstreamed to the holdco [S13].

bias_and_tone.note: The prose tracks the price. The stock rose 6.8% to Rp5,000 and the target rose 7.0% to Rp5,041 while the NAV fell slightly and the expected return fell to 8.8%; the rating is insulated from the price move because the discount is re-anchored to it. Section 4 claims the base "mixes sourced departures rather than a one-way haircut" and lists the observed discount as a conservative departure, but the discount is the most optimistic input in the model (below the card range and the peer set). Section 5 admits the target "overstates a true-bear-weighted target" and still publishes it.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The macro deck is read consistently: rupiah 18,350 FY2027E, policy rate 5.75%, inflation 3.28%, real GDP 5.29%, terminal growth 4% below the 5% cap and nominal GDP. No benchmark, realisation, royalty or cost-currency variable applies to a domestic distribution and lending conglomerate. The ASII discount outlier against the peer set is a valuation input, carried under assumption_realism, not a deck mismatch.

conservatism_audit.note: The stack is not signed and the report calls it balanced. Below the last actual or exit rate: auto block 9M x 4/3 vs the Q3 exit (about Rp453/share of NAV), Q4 net income 12% below the Q3 clean run-rate, financing ROE 16.0% vs 16.9% annualised, buyback truncated at 2.0%, FY2027E revenue growth 5% vs 8.6% implied nominal GDP. Offset upward: FY2026E minority 11% vs 18.5% audited, FY2027E gross-margin reversion 21.70% to 22.09%, and the 16.46% discount below the card range. The report lists the auto block as an offset when it is a haircut. No net value effect is shown.

calibration.note: The engine emits no blocking flag. The -1.38pp EBITDA-margin gap (16.11% FY2026E vs 17.48% FY2025A) is fully explained by the sourced nine-month cost base: SG&A at 11.22% vs the FY2025 10.14% (1.08pp) and gross margin 21.70% vs 22.09% (0.39pp) [S15, S6]. The two scenario BLOCK flags are marked justified only by the method card, not a registered source; that asymmetry is challenged under assumption_realism.

signoff.notes: Peer comps: ASII holdco_discount 30% is the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT midpoint and is identical to ADRO/BRPT/CUAN 30%; the report states the reason (card base rate, no dated narrowing catalyst, untested related-party flow) and shows the 20% bull and 40% bear endpoints, so the identical input is disclosed, not templated. DSSA/TOBA 40% and BNBR 38% differ on governance and liquidity; ABMM 68.9% is the distress outlier and not a template. WACC 11.93% (COE 14.63%) is the top of the 10.3-12.0% peer band, explained by the 1.32 levered beta and financial-services gearing. The 30% is justified as the most-likely base rate, not merely cautious: method-mandated, independent of the price, with the 21.05% market-implied discount at the range floor; the residual caution is that the base assumes a 9pp widening and the vector puts 75% on widening versus 25% on persistence. FATAL/MATERIAL: C1-C13 all answered on substance, with dated 6 Nov stake marks and the SOTP as an output; none outstanding. QC Q1 NOT cleared: section 5 still says the financing bear removes Rp1,160bn of income capitalised at the segment multiple (about Rp10.2tn) against the about Rp6.2tn de-rate to book, a two-thirds overstatement; next-version fix, not rating-changing. QC Q2 NOT cleared: the bull is still labelled as the buyback narrowing the discount to the floor when 20% is about 1pp from the 21.05% print; relabel as persistence next version. Lint PASS, 3,277 words. Batch bias: ASII is alone at sign-off; current expected TR is 2.5% (not the 8-9% of v5), below the peer HOLD cluster (ADRO 1.3%, BNBR 1.4%, TOBA 7.0%) and opposite ABMM ADD; peer ratings span ADD/SELL/HOLD and the discount is the card midpoint rather than a shared bear path, so the HOLD is not a shared-input defect.

bias.note: The 30% base is the method card midpoint applied to the marks, not the price; the price-derived 21.05% is reported only as what the print implies, so the largest headwind is method-mandated rather than an unsourced haircut. The operating departures are signed and net mildly optimistic, all sourced: auto at the Q3 exit (+Rp317/share, October 81,482 vs Q3 monthly 80,673 [S20, F101, F102]), buyback -4.0% FY2027E (+Rp100/share, Rp10.0tn/11 months [S14, F65]), against the disclosed Q4 clean profit 12% below the Q3 run-rate and the 16.0% financing ROE (-Rp145/share). The probability vector is mildly cautious (Q2) but not rating-changing: bull 35%/bear 20% gives about Rp4,851, still HOLD.

recomputed.item: UNTR stake value (0.6212 x Rp23,025 x 3,493.09m)

findings.finding: Section 5 says a repeat of the H1 provisioning pace "would remove about Rp1,160bn of annualised income capitalised at the segment multiple". At the 8.75x segment multiple that reads as about Rp10.2tn of value, but the de-rate-to-book arithmetic the bear narrative discloses is about Rp6.2tn (Rp62,601bn mark less Rp56,453bn book); the multiple itself de-rates to 1.0x book, so capitalising the income loss at the old multiple overstates the disclosed bear depth by roughly two-thirds.

The bull's 20% discount destination is only about 1pp below the 21.05% the Rp5,000 price already implies, so the bull is the discount-persistence case, not a narrowing that "requires the undated buyback to be read as [a catalyst]" [S0, S15]. As labelled, 75% of the probability mass sits on a 9-19pp widening from the observed print (base 30%, bear 40%) while the no-change case gets the smallest weight at 25%; the report's own bull rationale therefore understates the bull's likelihood.

The financial-services block normalises the sustainable ROE to 16.0% against the 16.9% annualised 9M actual (Rp7,152bn x 4/3 over Rp56,453bn of segment equity [S15, F69, F83, F74]). The H1 charge cited (Rp1,160bn [S5, F35]) is already inside the nine-month actual, so the 0.9pp haircut requires a fourth-quarter provisioning step-up above the nine-month pace that no source states. Worth about Rp119/share, 2.5% of the target - material to a HOLD/ADD boundary but not to the rating here.

P/E Rp5,425 and P/BV Rp6,686 sit 22% and 51% above the 96%-weighted SOTP [S0]; the 2%/2% weights are defensible under VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT (SOTP primary), but the weights.changed justification cites [S0, S15], neither of which speaks to the method weights - the supporting authority is the method card and the red team, not those sources.

FY2025A net debt in the model is Rp56,315bn [S0], while the FY2025 LK gearing note shows Rp57,680bn at 31 December 2025 [S15 page 113]. The 2.4% gap is below the 5% threshold, is not target-driving (the bridge uses parent net debt of Rp2,824bn), and the report cites S0 for it.
